May the LORD, the God of Israel, be blessed from ages past to ages to come!
Then all the people said, “Amen!” and praised the LORD.

Worship before the ark and at Gibeon

So David left Asaph and his fellow Levites there before the ark of the covenant of the LORD, to serve before the ark regularly, as each day’s work required. He also left Obed-Edom and their relatives, sixty-eight in all, and Obed-Edom son of Jeduthun and Hosah as gatekeepers. He left the priest Zadok and his fellow priests at the high place in Gibeon, before the tabernacle of the LORD, to offer burnt offerings to the LORD on the altar of burnt offering regularly, morning and evening, according to all that is written in the law of the LORD that he laid down for Israel. With them were Heman and Jeduthun and the rest of those chosen and named one by one to give thanks to the LORD, for his loyal love lasts forever. Heman and Jeduthun had with them trumpets and cymbals for the players to sound, and the instruments for the song of God. The sons of Jeduthun were at the gate. Then all the people went home, each to their own house, and David turned back to bless his household.

fields.title: 1 Chronicles 17
fields.body_html:
God’s promise to David

When David was settled in his house, he said to Nathan the prophet, “Look, I live in a house of cedar, but the ark of the covenant of the LORD stays under tent curtains.” Nathan said to David, “Do all that you have in mind, for God is with you.”

But that same night the word of God came to Nathan: “Go and tell my servant David, ‘The LORD says this: You are not the one who will build me the house to live in. I have not lived in a house from the day I brought Israel up until this day. I have moved from one tent to another and from one tabernacle to another. Wherever I have moved about among all Israel, did I ever say a word to any of the judges of Israel that I commanded to shepherd my people, asking, “Why have you not built me a house of cedar?”‘ Now then, say this to my servant David: ‘The LORD of Armies says this: I took you from the pasture, from following the sheep, to be ruler over my people Israel. Wherever you have gone, I have been with you, and I have cut off all your enemies in front of you. Now I will make you a name like the names of the greatest people on earth. I will appoint a place for my people Israel and plant them there, so that they may live in their own place and not be troubled anymore. Wicked people will no longer wear them down as they did at the beginning, ever since the time I set judges over my people Israel. I will also bring all your enemies low. And I declare to you that the LORD will build you a house. When your days are complete and you go to be with your ancestors, I will raise up your offspring after you, one of your own sons, and I will make his kingdom firm. He is the one who will build me a house, and I will make his throne firm forever. I will be a father to him, and he will be a son to me. I will not take my faithful love away from him, as I took it away from the one who was before you. I will keep him in place over my house and my kingdom forever, and his throne will stand firm for all time.’” Nathan spoke to David in keeping with all these words and all this vision.

David’s prayer

Then King David went in and sat down before the LORD and said, “LORD God, who am I, and what is my house, that you have brought me as far as this? And as if this were too little in your sight, God, you have also spoken about the house of your servant far into the future. You have regarded me as a man of high rank, LORD God. What more can David say to you about the honor you have shown your servant? You know your servant. LORD, for the sake of your servant and as your own heart chose, you have done this great thing, to make all these great things known. LORD, there is no one like you, and there is no God but you, as all we have heard with our own ears tells us. Who is there like your people Israel, the one nation on earth that God went to redeem as his own people? You made a name for yourself by great and awesome deeds, driving out nations before your people, whom you redeemed from Egypt. You made your people Israel your own people forever, and you, LORD, have become their God. And now, LORD, let the word you have spoken about your servant and about his house stand firm forever, and do as you have said. Let it stand firm, and may your name be great forever, as people say, ‘The LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, is Israel’s God!’ And the house of your servant David will stand firm before you. For you, my God, have made it known to your servant that you will build him a house. That is why your servant has found the courage to pray before you. And now, LORD, you are God, and you have promised this good thing to your servant. So now it has pleased you to bless the house of your servant, so that it may last before you forever. For you, LORD, have blessed it, and it is blessed forever.”

fields.title: 1 Chronicles 18
fields.body_html:
David’s victories

Some time after this, David defeated the Philistines and brought them under his control. He took Gath and its villages out of the Philistines’ hands. He also defeated Moab, and the Moabites became subject to David and brought him tribute. David also defeated Hadadezer king of Zobah, toward Hamath, when Hadadezer went to set up his monument at the Euphrates River. David captured 1,000 chariots, 7,000 horsemen and 20,000 foot soldiers from him. He hamstrung all the chariot horses but kept enough of them for a hundred chariots. When the Arameans of Damascus came to help Hadadezer king of Zobah, David struck down 22,000 of the Arameans. Then David stationed garrisons in Aram of Damascus. The Arameans became David’s subjects and paid him tribute. The LORD gave David victory wherever he went. David took the gold shields that Hadadezer’s officials had carried, and brought them to Jerusalem. From Tibhath and Cun, towns of Hadadezer, David took a great quantity of bronze. With it Solomon made the bronze Sea, the pillars and the bronze articles.

When Tou king of Hamath heard that David had defeated the whole army of Hadadezer king of Zobah, he sent his son Hadoram to King David to greet him and congratulate him on fighting against Hadadezer and defeating him, for Hadadezer and Tou had often been at war. Hadoram brought all kinds of articles of gold, silver and bronze. King David dedicated these also to the LORD, as he had done with the silver and gold he had carried off from all the nations: from Edom, Moab, the Ammonites, the Philistines and Amalek. Abishai son of Zeruiah struck down 18,000 Edomites in the Valley of Salt. He stationed garrisons in Edom, and all the Edomites became subject to David. The LORD gave David victory wherever he went. So David reigned over all Israel, and he did what was just and right for all his people. Joab son of Zeruiah was commander of the army; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was recorder; Zadok son of Ahitub and Abimelech son of Abiathar were priests; Shavsha was secretary; Benaiah son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and the Pelethites; and David’s sons were the chief officials at the king’s side.

fields.title: 1 Chronicles 19
fields.body_html:
War with the Ammonites

Some time after this, Nahash king of the Ammonites died, and his son became king in his place. David said, “I will show faithful love to Hanun son of Nahash, because his father showed faithful love to me.” So David sent messengers to console Hanun over the death of his father. And David’s officials came to Hanun in the land of the Ammonites to console him. But the Ammonite officials said to Hanun, “Do you really think David is honoring your father by sending men to comfort you? Have his officials not come to you to explore, to overthrow, and to spy out the land?”

So Hanun seized David’s officials, shaved them, cut their garments off in the middle at the buttocks, and sent them on their way. When people came and told David what had happened to the men, he sent messengers to meet them, because the men were deeply ashamed. The king said, “Stay in Jericho until your beards have grown back, and then come home.” When the Ammonites saw that they had made themselves hateful to David, Hanun and the Ammonites sent about 37 tons of silver to hire chariots and horsemen from Aram-naharaim, Aram-maacah and Zobah. They hired 32,000 chariots and the king of Maacah with his army, and these came and camped near Medeba. The Ammonites also gathered from their cities and came out to fight.

When David heard about this, he sent out Joab with the whole army of warriors. The Ammonites marched out and formed their battle line at the city entrance, while the kings who had come took a separate position in the open country. Joab saw that the battle lines faced him both in front and behind. So he picked some of Israel’s best troops and lined them up against the Arameans. He put the rest of the troops under the command of his brother Abishai, and they lined up against the Ammonites. Joab said, “If the Arameans are too strong for me, you must come to my rescue. But if the Ammonites are too strong for you, I will rescue you. Be strong! Let us show courage for the sake of our people and the cities of our God. And may the LORD do what seems good to him.” Then Joab and the troops with him advanced to fight the Arameans, and the Arameans fled from him. When the Ammonites saw the Arameans flee, they also fled from Joab’s brother Abishai and withdrew into the city. Then Joab came to Jerusalem.

The Arameans are defeated

When the Arameans saw that they had been beaten by Israel, they sent messengers and brought out the Arameans who were beyond the Euphrates River, with Shophach, the commander of Hadadezer’s army, at their head. When David was told, he gathered all Israel, crossed the Jordan, came up to them, and formed his lines against them. David drew up his army for battle against the Arameans, and they fought with him. But the Arameans fled before Israel, and David killed 7,000 of their charioteers and 40,000 foot soldiers. He also put to death Shophach, the commander of their army. When those who were subject to Hadadezer saw that Israel had defeated them, they made peace with David and became his subjects. After this the Arameans were not willing to give the Ammonites any more help.

fields.title: 1 Chronicles 20
fields.body_html:
The capture of Rabbah

When the year came round again, at the season when kings set out on campaign, Joab led out the army in force. He ravaged the land of the Ammonites, then came and besieged Rabbah. But David himself stayed behind in Jerusalem. Joab attacked Rabbah and tore it down. David took the crown from their king’s head. He found that it weighed about 75 pounds of gold, and it held a precious stone. It was placed on David’s head. He also brought a great amount of plunder out of the city. He brought out the people who were in the city and cut them with saws, with iron picks and with more saws. David did the same to all the towns of the Ammonites. Then David and all the troops returned to Jerusalem.

Battles with the descendants of the Rapha

After this, war broke out with the Philistines at Gezer. That was when Sibbecai the Hushathite killed Sippai, one of the descendants of the Rephaim, and the Philistines were subdued. There was another battle with the Philistines, in which Elhanan son of Jair struck down Lahmi the brother of Goliath of Gath, whose spear had a shaft like a weaver’s beam. There was another battle at Gath, where there was a man of great size with six fingers on each of his hands and six toes on each of his feet, twenty-four altogether. He too was descended from the Rapha. When he taunted Israel, Jonathan son of Shimea, David’s brother, killed him. These were descendants of the Rapha in Gath, and they fell at the hands of David and his men.

fields.title: 1 Chronicles 21
fields.body_html:
David counts Israel

Satan rose up against Israel and stirred David up to count Israel. David told Joab and the troop commanders, “Go and count Israel from Beersheba to Dan, then bring me the report, so that I may know how many there are.” But Joab said, “May the LORD make his people a hundred times as many as they are! Are they not all, my lord the king, servants of my lord? Why does my lord wish for this? Why should it be a cause of guilt for Israel?” But the king’s order overruled Joab, so Joab went out and traveled through all Israel, and then came back to Jerusalem. Joab gave David the total of the people who had been registered: in all Israel there were 1,100,000 men who could handle a sword, and in Judah 470,000 men who could handle a sword. But Levi and Benjamin he left out of the count, for Joab found the king’s order hateful. God was displeased with this thing, and he struck Israel.

Then David said to God, “I have sinned greatly by doing this. Now please take away your servant’s guilt, for I have acted very foolishly.”

Gad brings David three choices

The LORD spoke to Gad, David’s seer: “Go and tell David, ‘The LORD says this: I am offering you three things. Choose one of them, and I will do it to you.’” So Gad went to David and said to him, “The LORD says this: ‘Take your choice: three years of famine; or three months of being swept away by your foes, with the sword of your enemies catching up with you; or three days of the sword of the LORD, a plague in the land, with the angel of the LORD bringing destruction throughout all the territory of Israel.’ Now decide what answer I should take back to the one who sent me.”

David said to Gad, “I am in deep distress. Let me fall into the hand of the LORD, for his mercy is very great; but do not let me fall into human hands.” So the LORD sent a plague on Israel, and 70,000 of the people of Israel died. Then God sent an angel to Jerusalem to destroy it. But as the angel was bringing destruction, the LORD saw it and relented from the disaster. He said to the angel who was bringing destruction, “Enough! Now hold back your hand.” The angel of the LORD was then standing by the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite.

David looked up and saw the angel of the LORD standing between earth and heaven, holding in his hand a drawn sword stretched out over Jerusalem. David and the elders, dressed in sackcloth, fell face down. David said to God, “Did I not give the command to count the people? It is I who have sinned and done great wrong. But these sheep, what have they done? LORD my God, please let your hand be against me and my father’s family, but do not let this plague strike your people.”

David buys Ornan’s threshing floor

Then the angel of the LORD told Gad to tell David to go up and set up an altar for the LORD on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite. So David went up as Gad had told him in the name of the LORD. Ornan turned and saw the angel, and the four sons with him hid themselves. Ornan had been threshing wheat. When David came to Ornan, Ornan looked and saw David. He went out from the threshing floor and bowed before David with his face to the ground. David said to Ornan, “Let me have the site of this threshing floor so that I can build an altar to the LORD on it. Sell it to me at its full price, so that the plague on the people may be stopped.” Ornan said to David, “Take it, and let my lord the king do whatever he thinks best. Look, I am giving you the oxen for burnt offerings, the threshing sledges for firewood, and the wheat for a grain offering. I give it all.” But King David said to Ornan, “No, I insist on paying you the full price for it. I will not take what is yours for the LORD, or offer a burnt offering at no cost to myself.” So David paid Ornan about 15 pounds of gold by weight for the site. David built an altar to the LORD there and sacrificed burnt offerings and peace offerings. He called on the LORD, and the LORD answered him by sending fire from heaven onto the altar of burnt offering.

Then the LORD gave the angel a command, and the angel put his sword back into its sheath. At that time, when David saw that the LORD had given him an answer at the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite, he offered his sacrifices there. Now at that time the tabernacle of the LORD, made by Moses in the wilderness, and the altar of burnt offering were at the high place in Gibeon. But David could not go there to seek God, because he was terrified of the sword of the angel of the LORD.

fields.title: 1 Chronicles 22
fields.body_html:
David prepares to build the temple

Then David declared, “Here is the house of the LORD God, and here is the altar of burnt offering for Israel.”

So David gave orders to gather the outsiders who were living in the land of Israel, and he set stonecutters to cut dressed stones for building the house of God. David provided a great deal of iron for nails for the doors of the gates and for clamps, and more bronze than could be weighed. There were also cedar logs beyond counting, for the Sidonians and the Tyrians had brought great quantities of cedar to David.

David said, “Solomon my son is young and inexperienced, and the house that is to be built for the LORD must be made great beyond measure, so that its fame and splendor reach all lands. So let me get things ready for it.” So before his death David laid up materials in great quantity. Then he summoned his son Solomon and charged him with building a house for the LORD, the God of Israel.

David’s charge to Solomon

David said to Solomon, “My son, it was my own desire to build a house for the name of the LORD my God. But the word of the LORD came to me: ‘You have poured out blood in great amounts and waged great wars. You will not build a house for my name, because of all the blood you have poured out on the earth in my presence. Look, a son is to be born to you, and he will be a man of rest. I will grant him rest from all the enemies around him. For his name will be Solomon, and in his days I will give Israel peace and quiet. He is the one who will build a house for my name. He will be a son to me, and I will be a father to him, and I will make the throne of his kingdom over Israel firm forever.’ Now, my son, may the LORD be with you, so that you prosper as you build the house of the LORD your God, just as he promised concerning you. Above all, may the LORD grant you insight and understanding when he sets you over Israel, so that you keep the law of the LORD your God. Then you will succeed, if you are careful to carry out the statutes and the rulings that the LORD commanded Moses for Israel. Be strong and courageous. Do not fear or lose heart. Look, with hard toil I have provided for the house of the LORD about 7,500,000 pounds of gold and about 75,000,000 pounds of silver, and bronze and iron beyond weighing, there is so much of it. I have also provided timber and stone, and you are to add to them. You also have workers in great numbers: stonecutters, craftsmen in stone and wood, and every kind of worker skilled for every task. The gold and silver, the bronze and iron, are beyond counting. Now get up and go to work, and may the LORD be with you.” Then David ordered all the officials of Israel to help his son Solomon. “Is not the LORD your God with you? Has he not given you rest on every side? For he has handed the people who lived in the land over to me, and the land lies subdued before the LORD and before his people. Now set your heart and soul on seeking the LORD your God. Get up and build the sanctuary of the LORD God, so that the ark of the covenant of the LORD and the sacred vessels of God can be brought into the house that is to be built for the name of the LORD.”

fields.title: 1 Chronicles 23
fields.body_html:
The Levites are counted and given their work

When David was old and had lived a full life, he made his son Solomon king over Israel. He gathered together all the officials of Israel, and the priests and the Levites. The Levites who were thirty years old and over were counted, and the total, counted man by man, was 38,000. David said, “Of these, 24,000 are to direct the work on the house of the LORD, and 6,000 are to serve as officials and judges, 4,000 are to be gatekeepers, while 4,000 are to praise the LORD, playing the instruments I made for giving praise.” David organized them into divisions by the sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath and Merari.

The Gershonites: Ladan and Shimei.

The sons of Ladan: Jehiel the chief, Zetham and Joel, three in all.

The sons of Shimei: Shelomoth, Haziel and Haran, three in all. These were the heads of the families of Ladan.

The sons of Shimei: Jahath, Zina, Jeush and Beriah. These were the sons of Shimei, four in all. Jahath was the first and Zizah the second. Jeush and Beriah had few sons, so they were counted as a single family with one assignment.

The sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron and Uzziel, four in all.

The sons of Amram: Aaron and Moses. Aaron was set apart, he and his sons for all time, to consecrate the most holy things, to burn offerings before the LORD, to minister to him, and to bless in his name forever. As for Moses the man of God, his sons were counted as part of the tribe of Levi. The sons of Moses: Gershom and Eliezer. The sons of Gershom: Shebuel the chief. The sons of Eliezer: Rehabiah the chief. Eliezer had no other sons, but Rehabiah’s sons were very many. The sons of Izhar: Shelomith the chief.

The sons of Hebron: Jeriah the first, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third and Jekameam the fourth. The sons of Uzziel: Micah the first and Isshiah the second.

The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. The sons of Mahli: Eleazar and Kish. Eleazar died without sons; he had only daughters. Their relatives, the sons of Kish, married them. The sons of Mushi: Mahli, Eder and Jeremoth, three in all. These were the descendants of Levi by their ancestral houses, the heads of the families as they were registered, listed by name one by one. They did the work of serving in the house of the LORD, from twenty years old and up. For David said, “The LORD, the God of Israel, has given his people rest, and he has made his home in Jerusalem forever. So the Levites also no longer need to carry the tabernacle or any of the things used in its service.” So, by David’s last instructions, the descendants of Levi were counted from twenty years old and up. Their duty was to assist the sons of Aaron in the service of the house of the LORD: to have charge of the courts and the side rooms, the cleansing of all the holy things, and the work of serving in the house of God, and for the bread set out in rows, the fine flour for the grain offering, the unleavened wafers, what was baked on the griddle and what was mixed with oil, and all the measures of quantity and size, and to stand each morning to give thanks and praise to the LORD, and to do the same in the evening, and to help whenever burnt offerings were offered to the LORD on Sabbaths, at new moons and at the appointed festivals, in the numbers the rules set for them, regularly before the LORD, So they carried out their duties for the tent of meeting and for the holy place, and served their relatives the sons of Aaron, in the service of the house of the LORD.

fields.title: 1 Chronicles 24
fields.body_html:
The divisions of the priests

The descendants of Aaron were grouped in divisions as follows. Aaron’s sons were Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar. But Nadab and Abihu died in their father’s lifetime, leaving no sons, and Eleazar and Ithamar served as the priests. With the help of Zadok, a descendant of Eleazar, and Ahimelech, a descendant of Ithamar, David divided them into their appointed order for their service. Eleazar’s descendants were found to have more leading men than Ithamar’s, so they divided them this way: sixteen heads of ancestral families from Eleazar’s descendants, and eight ancestral families from Ithamar’s. They divided them by lot, one group the same as the other, because there were officials of the sanctuary and officials of God among the descendants of Eleazar and among the descendants of Ithamar.

Shemaiah son of Nethanel, the scribe, a Levite, recorded them in the presence of the king and the officials, Zadok the priest, Ahimelech son of Abiathar, and the heads of the priestly and Levite families. One ancestral family was drawn for Eleazar, and one drawn for Ithamar.

The first lot fell to Jehoiarib, the second to Jedaiah, the third to Harim, the fourth to Seorim, the fifth to Malchijah, the sixth to Mijamin, the seventh to Hakkoz, the eighth to Abijah, the ninth to Jeshua, the tenth to Shecaniah, the eleventh to Eliashib, the twelfth to Jakim, the thirteenth to Huppah, the fourteenth to Jeshebeab, the fifteenth to Bilgah, the sixteenth to Immer, the seventeenth to Hezir, the eighteenth to Ha-Pizzez, the nineteenth to Pethahiah, the twentieth to Jehezkel, the twenty-first to Jachin, the twenty-second to Gamul, the twenty-third to Delaiah, the twenty-fourth to Maaziah.

This was their appointed order for their service when they came into the house of the LORD, following the rule given them through Aaron their ancestor, as the LORD, the God of Israel, had commanded him.

The rest of the Levites

As for the rest of the descendants of Levi: from the sons of Amram, Shubael; from the sons of Shubael, Jehdeiah. From Rehabiah: from the sons of Rehabiah, Isshiah was the chief. From the Izharites: Shelomoth; from the sons of Shelomoth, Jahath. The sons of Hebron: Jeriah the first, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third and Jekameam the fourth. The sons of Uzziel: Micah; from the sons of Micah, Shamir. Micah’s brother: Isshiah; from the sons of Isshiah, Zechariah. The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi; and the sons of Jaaziah, his son. The descendants of Merari through his son Jaaziah: Shoham, Zaccur and Ibri. From Mahli: Eleazar, who had no sons. From Kish: the sons of Kish, Jerahmeel. The sons of Mushi: Mahli, Eder and Jerimoth. These were the descendants of the Levites by their ancestral families. These also cast lots, just as their relatives the descendants of Aaron had done, in the presence of King David, Zadok, Ahimelech, and the heads of the priestly and Levite families. The ancestral family of the head was treated just like that of his younger brother.

fields.title: 1 Chronicles 25
fields.body_html:
The temple musicians

David and the commanders of the army set apart for the service the sons of Asaph, Heman and Jeduthun, who prophesied with lyres, harps and cymbals. This is the list of the men who did the work of their service: Of the sons of Asaph: Zaccur, Joseph, Nethaniah and Asarelah. These sons of Asaph worked under Asaph’s direction, and he prophesied at the king’s direction. Of Jeduthun, the sons of Jeduthun: Gedaliah, Zeri, Jeshaiah, Hashabiah and Mattithiah, six, under the direction of their father Jeduthun, who prophesied with the lyre, giving thanks and praise to the LORD.

Of Heman, the sons of Heman: Bukkiah, Mattaniah, Uzziel, Shebuel, Jerimoth, Hananiah, Hanani, Eliathah, Giddalti, Romamti-Ezer, Joshbekashah, Mallothi, Hothir and Mahazioth. All these were sons of Heman, the king’s seer, in keeping with God’s promises to lift up his horn; God gave Heman fourteen sons and three daughters. All these were under their father’s direction for the music in the house of the LORD, with cymbals, harps and lyres, in the service of God’s house. Asaph, Jeduthun and Heman served at the king’s direction. Their number, together with their relatives who were trained in singing to the LORD, all of them skilled, was 288. They cast lots for their duties on equal terms, small and great alike, teacher and pupil alike.

The first lot fell for Asaph to Joseph; the second to Gedaliah, he and his relatives and his sons, twelve. The third to Zaccur, his sons and his relatives, twelve. The fourth to Izri, his sons and his relatives, twelve. The fifth to Nethaniah, his sons and his relatives, twelve. The sixth to Bukkiah, his sons and his relatives, twelve. The seventh to Jesarelah, his sons and his relatives, twelve. The eighth to Jeshaiah, his sons and his relatives, twelve. The ninth to Mattaniah, his sons and his relatives, twelve. The tenth to Shimei, his sons and his relatives, twelve. The eleventh to Azarel, his sons and his relatives, twelve. The twelfth to Hashabiah, his sons and his relatives, twelve. The thirteenth to Shubael, his sons and his relatives, twelve. The fourteenth to Mattithiah, his sons and his relatives, twelve. The fifteenth to Jeremoth, his sons and his relatives, twelve. The sixteenth to Hananiah, his sons and his relatives, twelve. The seventeenth to Joshbekashah, his sons and his relatives, twelve. The eighteenth to Hanani, his sons and his relatives, twelve. The nineteenth to Mallothi, his sons and his relatives, twelve. The twentieth to Eliathah, his sons and his relatives, twelve. The twenty-first to Hothir, his sons and his relatives, twelve. The twenty-second to Giddalti, his sons and his relatives, twelve. The twenty-third to Mahazioth, his sons and his relatives, twelve. The twenty-fourth to Romamti-Ezer, his sons and his relatives, twelve.

fields.title: 1 Chronicles 26
fields.body_html:
The gatekeepers

The divisions of the gatekeepers were these. From the Korahites came Meshelemiah son of Kore, of the sons of Asaph. Meshelemiah had sons: Zechariah the firstborn, Jediael the second, Zebadiah the third, Jathniel the fourth, Elam the fifth, Jehohanan the sixth and Eliehoenai the seventh. Obed-Edom had sons: Shemaiah the firstborn, Jehozabad the second, Joah the third, Sachar the fourth, Nethanel the fifth, Ammiel the sixth, Issachar the seventh and Peullethai the eighth. For God had blessed him.

Sons were also born to his son Shemaiah, and they were leaders in their father’s family, for they were mighty warriors. The sons of Shemaiah: Othni, Rephael, Obed and Elzabad, whose relatives Elihu and Semachiah were able men. All these were descendants of Obed-Edom. They, their sons and their relatives were able men, strong enough for the work: sixty-two from Obed-Edom’s family. Meshelemiah had sons and relatives who were able men, eighteen in all.

Hosah, one of the descendants of Merari, had sons: Shimri the chief (though he was not the firstborn, his father made him chief), Hilkiah the second, Tebaliah the third and Zechariah the fourth. Hosah’s sons and relatives numbered thirteen in all. These divisions of the gatekeepers, under their chief men, had duties of service in the house of the LORD, just as their relatives did. They cast lots for each gate by their ancestral families, the small and the great alike.

The lot for the east fell to Shelemiah. Then they cast lots for his son Zechariah, a wise counselor, and his lot came out for the north.

Obed-Edom’s lot was the south, and his sons were given the storehouse. Shuppim and Hosah were given the west, with the Shallecheth Gate on the road that goes up. Each guard post had a matching post. On the east there were six Levites, on the north four a day, on the south four a day, and at the storehouse they served two by two. At the Parbar on the west there were four at the road and two at the Parbar itself. These were the divisions of the gatekeepers among the descendants of Korah and of Merari. Of the Levites, Ahijah had charge of the treasuries of the house of God and of the treasuries for the dedicated gifts. From the sons of Ladan, Gershonites descended through Ladan and heads of the ancestral families of Ladan the Gershonite, came Jehieli. The sons of Jehieli, Zetham and his brother Joel, had charge of the treasuries in the house of the LORD. From the Amramites, the Izharites, the Hebronites and the Uzzielites: Shebuel son of Gershom, son of Moses, was chief officer in charge of the treasuries. His relatives through Eliezer were Rehabiah his son, Jeshaiah his son, Joram his son, Zichri his son and Shelomoth his son. This Shelomoth and his relatives were in charge of all the treasuries of the dedicated gifts that King David had dedicated, along with the heads of ancestral families, the commanders of thousands and of hundreds, and the commanders of the army. They dedicated part of the plunder from the battles to support the house of the LORD. Everything dedicated by Samuel the seer, Saul son of Kish, Abner son of Ner and Joab son of Zeruiah, every dedicated gift, was in the care of Shelomith and his relatives.

Officials and judges outside the temple

From the Izharites, Chenaniah and his sons were given duties outside the temple, over Israel, as officials and judges. From the Hebronites, Hashabiah and his relatives, 1,700 able men, had oversight of Israel on the west side of the Jordan, for all the work of the LORD and the king’s service. Jerijah was chief among the Hebronites, by the genealogies of their ancestral families. In the fortieth year of David’s reign a search was made, and mighty warriors from among them were found at Jazer in Gilead. Jerijah’s relatives, 2,700 able men, were heads of ancestral families. King David put them in charge of the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh in every matter concerning God and every matter concerning the king.

fields.title: 1 Chronicles 27
fields.body_html:
The army divisions

This is the list of the Israelites by number: heads of families, commanders of thousands and of hundreds, and the officials under them, who served the king in every matter that concerned the divisions. One division came on duty and another went off duty month by month throughout the year, and each division had 24,000 men.

In charge of the first division, for the first month, was Jashobeam son of Zabdiel. His division numbered 24,000. He was a descendant of Perez and was chief of all the army commanders for the first month. In charge of the division for the second month was Dodai the Ahohite, and Mikloth was the chief officer of his division. His division numbered 24,000.

The third army commander, for the third month, was Benaiah son of Jehoiada the priest, who served as chief. His division numbered 24,000. This was the Benaiah who was a mighty warrior among the Thirty and was over the Thirty. His son Ammizabad was in charge of his division.

The fourth commander, for the fourth month, was Asahel the brother of Joab, and after him his son Zebadiah. His division numbered 24,000.

The fifth commander, for the fifth month, was Shamhuth the Izrahite. His division numbered 24,000.

The sixth commander, for the sixth month, was Ira son of Ikkesh the Tekoite. His division numbered 24,000.

The seventh commander, for the seventh month, was Helez the Pelonite, an Ephraimite. His division numbered 24,000.

The eighth commander, for the eighth month, was Sibbecai the Hushathite, a Zerahite. His division numbered 24,000.

The ninth commander, for the ninth month, was Abiezer the Anathothite, a Benjaminite. His division numbered 24,000.

The tenth commander, for the tenth month, was Maharai the Netophathite, a Zerahite. His division numbered 24,000.

The eleventh commander, for the eleventh month, was Benaiah the Pirathonite, an Ephraimite. His division numbered 24,000.

The twelfth commander, for the twelfth month, was Heldai the Netophathite, of the family of Othniel. His division numbered 24,000.

The leaders of the tribes

Over the tribes of Israel were these: for the Reubenites, the ruler was Eliezer son of Zichri; for the Simeonites, Shephatiah son of Maacah;

for Levi, Hashabiah son of Kemuel; for Aaron, Zadok;

for Judah, Elihu, one of David’s brothers; for Issachar, Omri son of Michael;

for Zebulun, Ishmaiah son of Obadiah; for Naphtali, Jerimoth son of Azriel;

for the Ephraimites, Hoshea son of Azaziah; for the half-tribe of Manasseh, Joel son of Pedaiah;

for the half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead, Iddo son of Zechariah; for Benjamin, Jaasiel son of Abner;

for Dan, Azarel son of Jeroham. These were the leaders over Israel’s tribes. David did not count those who were twenty years old or younger, because the LORD had promised to make Israel as many as the stars in the sky. Joab son of Zeruiah began to count them but did not finish. Because of this, wrath came on Israel, and the number was not entered in the record of the History of King David.

The managers of the king’s property

Azmaveth son of Adiel was in charge of the king’s treasuries. Jonathan son of Uzziah was in charge of the storehouses out in the country, in the towns, in the villages and in the towers.

Ezri son of Chelub was in charge of the field workers who farmed the land. Shimei the Ramathite was in charge of the vineyards, and Zabdi the Shiphmite was in charge of the vineyards’ yield for the wine cellars.

Baal-hanan the Gederite was in charge of the olive trees and the sycamore-fig trees in the Shephelah, and Joash was in charge of the stores of olive oil.

Shitrai the Sharonite was in charge of the herds that grazed in Sharon, and Shaphat son of Adlai over the herds in the valleys.

Obil the Ishmaelite was in charge of the camels, and Jehdeiah the Meronothite was in charge of the donkeys.

Jaziz the Hagrite was in charge of the flocks. All these were the officials in charge of King David’s property. Jonathan, David’s uncle, was a counselor; he was a man of understanding and a scribe. Jehiel son of Hachmoni attended the king’s sons. Ahithophel was counselor to the king, and Hushai the Archite was the king’s friend. After Ahithophel came Jehoiada son of Benaiah and Abiathar. Joab was the commander of the king’s army.

fields.title: 1 Chronicles 28
fields.body_html:
David’s instructions for the temple

David gathered all the officials of Israel at Jerusalem: the officials of the tribes, the commanders of the divisions that served the king, the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds, and the officials who managed all the property and livestock that belonged to the king and his sons, along with the court officials, the warriors and every mighty warrior. King David stood up and said, “Hear me, my brothers and my people. I had set my heart on building a house where the ark of the covenant of the LORD could rest, the footstool of our God, and I made preparations for building it. But God said to me, ‘You will not build a house for my name, for you are a man of war and you have poured out blood.’ Still, the LORD, the God of Israel, chose me from my whole family to be king over Israel forever. He chose Judah to lead, and among the people of Judah he chose my father’s family, and from my father’s sons it pleased him to make me king over all Israel. And of all my sons, and the LORD has given me many, he has chosen my son Solomon to sit on the throne of the LORD’s kingdom over Israel. He said to me, ‘Your son Solomon is the one who will build my house and my courts. I have chosen him as my son, and I will be a father to him. I will make his kingdom firm forever if he holds firmly to doing my commandments and my rulings, as he does today.’ So now, before the eyes of all Israel, the assembly of the LORD, and with our God listening, I charge you: keep all the commandments of the LORD your God and seek them out, so that you may keep possession of the good land and leave it to your descendants after you as their inheritance forever.

As for you, my son Solomon, know your father’s God, and serve him with an undivided heart and a willing soul, for the LORD searches every heart and understands every intention behind people’s thoughts. If you seek him, he will let you find him; but if you abandon him, he will reject you forever. Consider this now: the LORD has chosen you to build a house to be the sanctuary. Be strong and do the work.”

The plans for the temple

Then David gave his son Solomon the plans for the porch of the temple, its buildings, its treasuries, its upper rooms, its inner rooms and the room for the mercy seat, and the plans for everything he had in mind: the courts of the LORD’s house and all the rooms around them, the treasuries of God’s house and the treasuries for the dedicated gifts, for the priests’ and Levites’ divisions, for all the work of serving in the LORD’s house, and for all the articles used in the service of the LORD’s house, the weight of gold for all the gold articles used in each kind of service, and the weight of silver for all the silver articles used in each kind of service, the weight of the gold lampstands and their gold lamps, with the weight for each lampstand and its lamps; and the weight of the silver lampstands, for each lampstand and its lamps, according to the use of each lampstand, the weight of gold for each of the tables for the rows of holy bread, and silver for the silver tables, the pure gold for the forks, the basins and the pitchers; the weight of gold for each gold bowl, and the weight of silver for each silver bowl, and the weight of refined gold for the altar of incense; and the plan for the chariot, the gold cherubim that spread their wings and cover the ark of the covenant of the LORD. “All this,” David said, “is in writing from the hand of the LORD upon me. He made me understand all the details of the plan.”

David said to his son Solomon, “Be strong and courageous, and do the work. Do not be afraid or lose heart, for the LORD God, my God, is with you. He will not let go of you or abandon you until you have finished all the work for the service of the LORD’s house. Look, here are the divisions of the priests and the Levites for every kind of service in the house of God. Every willing person with skill for any kind of service will be with you in all the work, and the officials and all the people will do whatever you command.”

fields.title: 1 Chronicles 29
fields.body_html:
Gifts for the temple

King David then spoke to the whole assembly: “God has chosen my son Solomon alone, but he is young and inexperienced, and the task is great, because this palace is not for a human being but for the LORD God. With all my strength I have provided for the house of my God: gold for the things of gold and silver for the things of silver, bronze and iron for what is to be made of them, and timber for the woodwork, along with onyx stones and stones for setting, dark antimony stones and stones of many colors, every kind of precious stone, and alabaster in great quantity. Moreover, because I delight in the house of my God, I am giving my own treasure of gold and silver to the house of my God, over and above everything I have provided for the holy house: about 110 tons of gold, gold of Ophir, and about 260 tons of refined silver for covering the walls of the buildings, gold for the things of gold and silver for the things of silver, and for all the work to be done by craftsmen. Now who is willing to give freely and consecrate themselves today to the LORD?” Then the family leaders and the tribal leaders of Israel gave freely, together with the commanders over thousands and hundreds and the officials who managed the king’s work. For the service of the house of God they gave about 190 tons and about 185 pounds of gold, about 375 tons of silver, about 675 tons of bronze and about 3,750 tons of iron. Any who owned precious stones handed them over to the treasury of the house of the LORD, in the care of Jehiel the Gershonite. The people rejoiced over these freewill gifts, for with a whole heart they had given freely to the LORD. King David also rejoiced with great joy.

David’s prayer of praise

Then David blessed the LORD in the sight of the whole assembly. David said, “Blessed are you, LORD, God of our father Israel, from everlasting to everlasting. To you, LORD, belong the greatness, the power, the glory, the victory and the majesty; indeed everything in heaven and on earth is yours. The kingdom is yours, LORD, and you are lifted high as head over all. Riches and honor come from you; you rule over everything. In your hand are power and might, and it is in your hand to make anyone great and to give strength to all. And now, our God, we give you thanks and praise your glorious name. But who am I, and who are my people, that we should have the means to give as freely as this? Everything comes from you; what we have given you came from your own hand. For we are outsiders before you, and temporary settlers, as all our ancestors were. Our days on earth are like a shadow, with no hope of staying. LORD our God, all this wealth that we have gathered to build a house for your holy name has come from your hand, and every part of it belongs to you. My God, I know that you examine the heart and that uprightness pleases you. With an upright heart I have freely given all these things, and now I have watched your people gathered here give freely to you with joy. LORD, God of our ancestors Abraham, Isaac and Israel, keep this willingness forever in the purposes and thoughts of your people’s hearts, and set their hearts firmly on you. Give my son Solomon a whole heart to keep your commandments, your decrees and your statutes, to carry them all out, and to build the palace for which I have made preparations.”

Solomon is made king

Then David said to the whole assembly, “Now bless the LORD your God.” And the whole assembly blessed the LORD, the God of their ancestors. They bowed their heads and lay face down before the LORD and before the king. The next day they offered sacrifices to the LORD and burnt offerings to the LORD: 1,000 bulls, 1,000 rams and 1,000 lambs, each with its drink offering, and a great many sacrifices for all Israel. They ate and drank before the LORD that day with great joy. Then they made Solomon son of David king a second time and anointed him as ruler for the LORD, and Zadok as priest. So Solomon took his seat on the throne of the LORD as king, succeeding his father David. He prospered, and all Israel obeyed him. All the officials and the mighty warriors, and also all King David’s sons, pledged their loyalty to King Solomon. The LORD made Solomon exceedingly great in the sight of all Israel and gave him royal majesty such as no king over Israel before him had had.

The end of David’s reign

So David son of Jesse reigned over all Israel. His reign over Israel lasted forty years: seven of them he reigned in Hebron, and thirty-three in Jerusalem. He died at a good old age, having had his fill of days, riches and honor, and his son Solomon became king in his place. The acts of King David, from first to last, are written in the records of Samuel the seer, the records of Nathan the prophet and the records of Gad the seer, together with all his reign and his power, and the events that came upon him, upon Israel and upon all the kingdoms of the lands.

fields.title: Conclusion
fields.body_html:
For we are outsiders before you, and temporary settlers, as all our ancestors were. Our days on earth are like a shadow, with no hope of staying.

— 1 Chronicles 29:15

1 Chronicles ends with a funeral and a coronation, but its real ending is a prayer. Before he dies, David stands before the whole assembly, surrounded by the gold and silver given for a house he will never see, and confesses that none of it was ever his. The king who had everything calls himself and his people outsiders and temporary settlers, whose days pass like a shadow.

The question the book leaves with you

Chronicles was written for people who had been through the shadow. They had lost their king, their independence and Solomon’s temple, and they lived as a small province of a foreign empire. The book’s answer to them was not to look back in nostalgia, but to look up. The kingdom had always been the LORD’s: “The kingdom is yours, LORD.” David had only ever sat on “the throne of the LORD”. So the kingdom could not be lost when the throne was empty.

That leaves every reader with a question: what are you building for a God whose kingdom outlasts you? David spent his last years gathering stone and timber, training singers and gatekeepers and arranging the work of people not yet born, for a temple his son would finish. He did it gladly. And he asked his people to give “freely”, not because God needed their gold, but because “Everything comes from you; what we have given you came from your own hand.”

The New Testament gives David’s life the same shape. Paul, preaching in Pisidian Antioch, said that David, “after serving God’s purpose in his own generation, fell asleep in death” (Acts 13:36). To serve God’s purpose in one generation, and leave the rest to him, is what 1 Chronicles asks of its readers.

Where the story goes next

2 Chronicles begins where this book ends, with Solomon building the house his father prepared, on the threshing floor where David saw the angel stop. The cloud of glory fills it while the singers David appointed are singing the very words he gave them: “For he is good; his loyal love lasts forever.”

But the promise of chapter 17 reached further than Solomon. The prophets after the exile kept looking for a son of David whose throne would “stand firm for all time”. The New Testament says he came. The angel told Mary that God would give her son “the throne of David, his forefather”; Matthew begins his Gospel with Jesus, “the son of David”; and James, at the council in Jerusalem, heard in the prophets God’s promise, “I will build again the fallen tent of David” (Acts 15:16), being fulfilled as the nations came to seek the Lord.

And the temple David longed to build pointed beyond itself. Solomon would say at its dedication that the highest heaven cannot contain God. Jesus spoke of his own body as the temple, and the apostles of the church as God’s house built of living stones.

Where to go from here

1 Chronicles has been less preached than Samuel and Kings, but its prayers and its promise to David have fed the church, and the library holds some good companions to it:

  • On David’s kingdom. Hannah Whitall Smith’s Old Testament Types and Teachings, whose chapter “2 Samuel and 1 Chronicles: The Kingdom Under David” reads David’s reign as a picture of the soul that has taken Christ for its King; and Book XVII of Augustine’s The City of God, which argues that the promises God made to David about his son (1 Chronicles 17; 2 Samuel 7) are not fulfilled in Solomon but in Christ.
  • On the prayers of Chronicles (4:10, 5:20, 29:19). R. A. Torrey’s What the Bible Teaches, whose chapter on prayer gathers the prayers of Jabez, of the tribes east of the Jordan, and of David for his son among its Bible proofs.
  • On the lists themselves (4:23, 5:22). Charles H. Spurgeon’s Morning by Morning, whose readings for June 3 and June 8 find the gospel in two verses of the genealogies: the potters who lived with the king to do his work, and the battle that was God’s doing.
  • On the census (1 Chronicles 21). John Wesley’s sermon “National Sins and Miseries”, in his Sermons on Several Occasions, preached on David’s plea in 2 Samuel 24:17, “But what have these sheep done?”, and drawing on the account in 1 Chronicles 21.
  • On the worship David ordered (1 Chronicles 15–16). The Psalms in this library, in the same Open Word Bible translation, where the psalm of chapter 16 can be read in its full form in Psalms 96, 105 and 106; and Robert Murray M’Cheyne’s sermon Thanksgiving Obtains the Spirit (2 Chronicles 5:13–14), on the day the singers David had appointed praised the LORD and the cloud filled the temple.

You can also go the other way, from the text to the classics. Every reference to 1 Chronicles in this library can be tapped to read the verse, and the Scripture pages gather, chapter by chapter, what the great writers of the church have said about each passage of this book.

And then read on into 2 Chronicles, taking with you the words with which David handed over everything he had gathered:

But who am I, and who are my people, that we should have the means to give as freely as this? Everything comes from you; what we have given you came from your own hand.

— 1 Chronicles 29:14
